P12. No defensible cash-flow forecast gets to TSLA's $362.44 price. The mechanical DCF gives $33.17 (WACC 11.20%, all terminal checks passed). Its drivers are generous, not biased low: a 9.5% margin from year 1 against 4.6% in FY2025, growth rising to 23.7% by year 10 against -2.9% in FY2025, and a 19.5% terminal ROIC, though P02 found ROIC below WACC. My justified runs all pass the checks. Base (15-year) $25.62: growth recovers to 10% then fades, margin rises from 4% to 10%, sales-to-capital 1.8, terminal ROIC 12%. Bull (15-year) $111.20: growth fades from 25% to 4%, margin rises from 6% to 20%, terminal ROIC 20%. Bear (10-year) $15.04: 2% growth at a flat 4% margin. The reverse DCF says the price needs 57.6% annual revenue growth at the mechanical margin, and at mechanical growth no margin up to 90% gets there. A deliberate stress case needs $1.27T of revenue by year 10, a 25% margin and a 30% terminal ROIC. It fails two checks and still gives $347.32. That gap is the thesis: the price pays for autonomy, robotaxi and Optimus outcomes far beyond Tesla's best year, while revenue has stalled and margins have fallen for three years. EPV is $13.90 and the LBO ceiling $26.94. Monte Carlo around the mechanical drivers gives P10–P90 of $20.59–$51.38, with a 0.0007 chance of value above the price. LTM comps imply $13.02 (EV/EBITDA), $34.78 (P/E) and $45.35 (EV/revenue), indicative only with 4 usable peers. The most generous WACC/growth corner gives $49.23, so the discount rate doesn't decide it. Fair value: $15.04–$111.20, centred on $25.62. Limits: the Monte Carlo and the grid use mechanical drivers; fiscal-year comps and the 20-F and BYD peers were unavailable; future CEO-award dilution may be missing from the 3,949M share count.

P02. Fraud screens and cash backing look clean; the problem is weak, worsening core earnings, increasingly propped up by non-operating, mark-to-market and one-off items. In Q2 2026, operating income was $398M on revenue of $28,236M, while net income was $1,114M. The bridge: a $1.00B net gain on a $2.00B SpaceX stake (related party: Tesla's CEO also runs SpaceX; Level 2, $238M marketability discount), $422M of interest income and a $274M tax benefit from a California valuation-allowance release. In FY2025, pre-tax income ($5,278M) exceeded operating income ($4,355M), helped by $1,680M of interest income. Operating margin fell from 16.76% (FY2022) to 4.59% (FY2025). Gross profit slipped while R&D rose from $3,969M to $6,411M and SG&A from $4,800M to $5,834M (FY2023–FY2025). ROIC was 4.6% against an 11.2% WACC; incremental ROIC was -0.268. Regulatory-credit revenue fell $770M (28%) after OBBBA. The 2025 CEO award carries $9.82B of unrecognised expense for the probable milestone, plus $105.82B, $120.37B for milestones not judged probable, a catch-up-charge risk. In Q2 2026 the CEO exercised about 304.0M options under the 2018 award, so dilution is under way. Clean checks: Beneish M -2.89 (threshold -1.78), Montier C 3, accrual ratio -0.084 (operating cash $14,747M vs net income $3,794M), negligible goodwill and intangibles, 29 of 29 evaluated identity checks passed. The warranty reserve is being built, not released: 3.9% to 9.1% of revenue (FY2021–FY2025). Working capital is worsening: the cash conversion cycle went from -15.3 to +13.9 days, and inventory jumped in Q1 2026. Credit is very strong: $35.9B net cash, $44.1B liquidity, distance to default 12.39, $1,576M of debt due within a year.

1Cover and recommendation

Cover and recommendation P15_trade · 10/13 checklist

Recommendation (JUDGMENT, low certainty): NEUTRAL at 0-3 months, SHORT at 12 months, SHORT at 3-5 years. None is STRONG. Scores out of 100: long conviction 15, short conviction 60, certainty 30, volatility risk 85, fundamental quality 50, valuation attractiveness 5, momentum 35, sentiment 45, management and governance 35, bubble risk 80. The valuation gap is real and is not a units error. get_valuation gives an equity value of $131.0bn over 3.949bn diluted shares, which is $33.17 per share, and all terminal checks pass or have no data. Earnings power ($13.90) and the LBO ceiling ($26.94) are lower still. Every house percentile and every P13 scenario, including the $329.92 super-bull, is below $362.44. Certainty is low. The LTM peer set missed its minimum, there are 10 medium-impact snapshot gaps (none high), there is no weighted scenario value or horizon target, and the gap between value and price is about tenfold. That gap reflects Robotaxi, FSD and Optimus optionality, which a DCF cannot price. The edge comes from horizon, not information. Do not short into the Q3 2026 print (inferred late October 2026), because post-filing moves skew upward. Build the short in stages after it. The thesis is invalidated by two consecutive quarters of operating margin above the 9.52% mechanical driver together with positive, accelerating revenue growth. Liquidity does not constrain size: a $500m position is about 4% of 20-day ADV. There is no bid-ask spread, borrow fee or options pricing in the data. The engine returned no Kelly fraction, volatility-targeted size or dollar maximum loss, so sizing is qualitative: small, and beta-hedged (Blume beta 1.45). Time stop: review at FY2026 results (inferred late January 2027). Exit if the thesis has not progressed by the following annual report. Research output, not investment advice.

  • JUDGMENT Recommendation by horizon: NEUTRAL at 0-3 months, SHORT at 12 months, SHORT at 3-5 years. None is STRONG SHORT, because the certainty score (30) cannot support high conviction even with valuation attractiveness at 5. The different answers by horizon are deliberate. No near-term catalyst closes the gap to fundamental value (P13), and the post-filing reaction function skews upward, which argues against a short-dated short. confidence 0.45

2Executive summary

Executive summary P15_trade · 10/13 checklist
  • FACT The mechanical DCF gives an enterprise value of about $95.7bn and an equity value of about $131.0bn, or $33.17 per share on 3.949bn diluted shares. The terminal value is 71.2% of EV, against a 75% limit. Terminal ROIC is 19.50% against a WACC of 11.20%. Every terminal check that could be run passed. The TAM share and best-in-class margin checks could not be run because no TAM or best-in-class margin was supplied. mechanical_dcf terminal_checks
  • INFERENCE P10 asked for a check on units or share count. The check comes back clean: the per-share value follows directly from the equity value and the diluted share count. The roughly 91% gap between price and value (`mechanical_upside`) therefore comes from the drivers, not from the arithmetic. The drivers are a 9.52% flat operating margin and revenue growth starting at -2.93% and recovering toward the peer median. confidence 0.80
  • FACT Earnings power value is $13.90 per share and the LBO ceiling is $26.94 per share. earnings_power_per_share lbo_ceiling_per_share
  • INFERENCE Every independent value anchor points the same way. These are the mechanical DCF, earnings power, the LBO ceiling, the house Monte Carlo band (`house_p10` to `house_p90`) and all five P13 scenarios. The P13 super-bull ($329.92) still sits below the price, and it fails two checks. The market price therefore implies more than the most optimistic case the engine could write down. confidence 0.70
  • JUDGMENT The short thesis is a valuation-convergence thesis, and the timing is weak. TSLA's price has carried a narrative premium tied to autonomy and robotics, which no free-data DCF can value or falsify. Convergence could take years, or it might never happen if that optionality pays off. This is why short conviction is 60 and not higher. confidence 0.50

2aTear sheet

Tear sheet P15_trade · 10/13 checklist
  • JUDGMENT Long conviction is 15 (rests on P06, P12 and P13). Nothing fundamental supports the price, because every scenario sits below it. The score is not near zero because the upward post-filing reaction skew (P13) and the unvalued autonomy optionality give a long holder some tactical support. confidence 0.55
  • JUDGMENT Short conviction is 60 (rests on P06, P12 and P13 for valuation, P09 for positioning and P10 for the technicals). For the short: extreme overvaluation on every anchor, negative 12-1 momentum, and lagging SPY. Against it: no dated catalyst, upward-skewed earnings reactions, about 59.6% annual volatility (`annual_volatility`) that makes holding costly, and a controlling holder whose narrative can re-rate the stock. confidence 0.50
  • JUDGMENT Certainty is 30 (rests on P05, P06, P12 and P13 and the gap register). The LTM comps failed the five-peer minimum: only 4 peers were measurable, and TM, STLA, NIO, XPEV, LI and BYDDY were excluded (`comps_meets_minimum`). The fiscal-year table did meet its minimum (`fy_comps_meets_minimum`). There are 10 medium-impact and 2 low-impact snapshot gaps and no high-impact ones (`snapshot_gaps_medium`, `snapshot_gaps_low`, `snapshot_gaps_high`), plus 11 analysis gaps (`analysis_gaps`). Mechanical value and price differ by about a factor of ten. P13 computed no weighted scenario value or horizon target, and its scenario values differ from P12's by up to about $9. Certainty would be lower still if the mechanical checks had failed, but none did (`mechanical_checks_failed`). confidence 0.60
  • JUDGMENT Volatility risk is 85 (rests on P10). Annualised volatility is near 60%, the maximum drawdown is -73.6% (`max_drawdown`), and the historical CVaR is worse than the parametric figure, so the tails are fat. Beta rose to 2.20 over the trailing year. No 2008 replay or recovery times were computed, so this score probably understates the holding experience. confidence 0.65
  • JUDGMENT Fundamental quality is 50 (rests on P06, P10 and get_valuation). Positives: net cash (equity value exceeds EV in the DCF), a debt weight of only about 0.6% of capital, and a terminal ROIC of 19.5% above WACC. Negatives: factor loadings with strongly negative RMW and CMA, which is the profile of a low-profitability, heavily investing stock, and a 9.52% operating margin driver. Fifty means quality gives no edge either way. confidence 0.45
  • JUDGMENT Valuation attractiveness is 5 (rests on P06, P12, P13 and get_valuation). Each anchor sits about an order of magnitude below the price. The score is limited by the failed LTM peer set, which means relative valuation could not be cross-checked properly. confidence 0.60
  • JUDGMENT Momentum is 35 (rests on P10). The 12-1 momentum is negative, the stock is in the lower third of its 52-week range and below its 20-, 100- and 200-day averages, and ADX near 15 shows no trend. The momentum factor loading itself was not significant (t 1.54). confidence 0.50
  • JUDGMENT Sentiment is 45 (rests on P09). The composite is about -7 on a -100 to +100 scale, and short interest is low. All three sources were partial. 13F data is stale and contains 360 filer-error positions. There is no options, retail-flow or sell-side data. confidence 0.40
  • JUDGMENT Management and governance is 35 (rests on P08, P09 and P13). The negatives are a controlling holder with about 20.3% of shares and about 236m shares pledged, plus pending litigation: the $329m Benavides verdict under appeal, the FSD class-certification appeal and a Texas securities class action. Insider sales were small and almost all made under 10b5-1 plans. confidence 0.45
  • JUDGMENT Bubble risk is 80 (rests on P06, P10 and P13). The price exceeds even the super-bull scenario, which needs about $1.17T of revenue by year 10, and the factor R² is only 0.327, so most variance is stock-specific and driven by narrative. The score is not higher because positioning is not crowded (low short interest, sentiment near neutral). confidence 0.50
  • JUDGMENT Tear sheet pitch: TSLA trades at about ten times every fundamental anchor the engine can build. The DCF passes its terminal checks, and the gap is not an arithmetic error. The price is paying for autonomy and robotics optionality that no scenario short of a $1.17T-revenue super-bull justifies, and even that scenario falls short. The trade is a small, beta-hedged, long-dated short entered after the Q3 print, sized for 60% volatility rather than for the size of the gap. Thirty-second version: the gap is about tenfold, timing is poor and certainty is low, so short small, short late and hedge the market. confidence 0.50
  • JUDGMENT Top risks: (1) an autonomy or robotaxi milestone re-rates the optionality; (2) an upward post-earnings gap, given the skewed reaction function; (3) a high-beta rally in the broad market; (4) pledged-share dynamics or controlling-holder actions that move the price in either direction. Catalysts: Q3 2026 results (inferred late October 2026), FY2026 results (inferred late January 2027), and undated events (the Benavides appeal, the Ninth Circuit FSD ruling, Cybercab and Robotaxi milestones, regulatory actions). confidence 0.55

2cWhy now?

Why now? P13_scenarios · 10/11 checklist

I valued five scenarios with run_dcf, and every one is below the $362.44 price. Super-bear: $14.56. It fails the terminal-ROIC check on purpose, because it describes a business earning below its cost of capital. Bear: $16.22. Base: $24.74. Bull: $102.71. Super-bull: $329.92, which needs about $1.17T of revenue by year 10, a 25% margin and a 25% terminal ROIC, and fails two checks. Probabilities: 10%, 25%, 40%, 20% and 5%, summing to 100%. Under any weights the weighted value is below the price, since even the super-bull is. The engine computed no exact weighted figure or horizon targets, so those are gaps. My base, bear and bull are within about $9 of P12's $25.62, $15.04 and $111.20, likely because of driver settings P12's summary did not record. Skew: fundamental value has a long right tail, but against the price nearly all of it is downside. Meanwhile the post-filing reaction function shows up-moves larger than down-moves. Catalysts: Q3 2026 results are inferred for late October 2026 and FY2026 results for late January 2027. Undated: the Benavides appeal ($329m verdict; notice of appeal filed 16 March 2026), the Ninth Circuit FSD class-certification ruling (fully briefed), the Texas securities class action, Cybercab and Robotaxi milestones, and regulatory actions. Earnings preview: the market will trade on automotive gross margin (Q2 16.9%) and Robotaxi/FSD commentary. Beat-and-raise 25%, beat-and-hold 35%, miss-and-cut 40%; there is no consensus to compare against. Why now: no near-term catalyst closes a roughly 90% gap. Any edge is horizon, not information, and the upward post-filing skew argues against a short-dated position.

  • JUDGMENT Why now: nothing in the next two quarters is likely to close a gap where even a scenario that fails its checks lands below the price. Quarterly results, court rulings and product updates can move the stock, but the post-filing reaction is skewed upward. Any edge is horizon: years of autonomy and Optimus revenue failing to show up are what would close the gap, not better information. This argues for a long-horizon underweight or avoid stance, not a short timed to earnings. confidence 0.65

3Variant perception

There is no consensus estimate in any free source, so “where we differ from consensus” is an argument against the engine’s own reading of the price rather than against a published number.

Variant perception P13_scenarios · 10/11 checklist
  • JUDGMENT Variant perception: the market prices Tesla as an autonomy and robotics platform. My view is that the price needs roughly the super-bull path, about $1.2T of revenue by year 10 at a 25% margin with returns that fail plausibility checks, to be worth what it costs. I put about 5% on that path. The difference is about the probability of the autonomy outcome, not about the car business, where the market and I probably agree. confidence 0.60

4Business model and moat

Business model and moat P01_business · 14/16 checklist

Tesla reports two segments: automotive (which includes services and other) and energy generation and storage. FY2025 revenue was $94,827m, with engine-computed growth of -0.029306991503736307. Automotive sales were $65,821m, regulatory credits $1,993m, leasing $1,712m, services and other $12,530m and energy $12,771m. By geography: US $47,627m, China $20,962m, other international $26,238m. Most revenue comes from one-off vehicle sales to consumers: 1.64m deliveries against 1.66m produced in 2025. Cash deliveries fell about 8% and the average selling price fell on mix and bigger incentives. Regulatory-credit revenue is shrinking. It fell 28% in 2025 and 67% in Q2 2026 after OBBBA restricted credit programmes, and remaining performance obligations fell $3.84bn to $841m. Two lines are growing: energy (revenue up 27%, 46.7 GWh deployed, gross margin 29.8%) and services and other (up 19%). Deferred software revenue rose to $3,867m, but new additions fell to $1,083m. The warranty accrual rose to $8,607m, including $1,127m of upward revisions to warranties already on the books. Days of inventory eased to 57.149962049579976. In H1 2026, revenue rose 21% and automotive sales 24% on about 18% more cash deliveries. Total automotive gross margin was 18.7% for H1 but 16.9% in Q2. Moat scores (JUDGMENT): scale 3, cost advantage 2, brand 2, network effects 1, switching costs 1, IP 1, regulatory licences 0. Value drivers for P12/P13: (1) Model 3/Y deliveries; (2) automotive selling price net of incentives; (3) automotive gross margin excluding credits; (4) energy storage GWh and Megapack price and cost; (5) FSD and Robotaxi software revenue; (6) growth and margin in services and other; (7) how fast regulatory credits run off; (8) AI-driven R&D spend. Main gaps: margin and revenue excluding credits (not computed by the engine), dollar selling price, cost per vehicle, warranty cost per unit, FSD attach rate, energy remaining performance obligations, and order backlog.

5Financial forensics

Financial forensics P02_forensics · 10/10 checklist

Fraud screens and cash backing look clean; the problem is weak, worsening core earnings, increasingly propped up by non-operating, mark-to-market and one-off items. In Q2 2026, operating income was $398M on revenue of $28,236M, while net income was $1,114M. The bridge: a $1.00B net gain on a $2.00B SpaceX stake (related party: Tesla's CEO also runs SpaceX; Level 2, $238M marketability discount), $422M of interest income and a $274M tax benefit from a California valuation-allowance release. In FY2025, pre-tax income ($5,278M) exceeded operating income ($4,355M), helped by $1,680M of interest income. Operating margin fell from 16.76% (FY2022) to 4.59% (FY2025). Gross profit slipped while R&D rose from $3,969M to $6,411M and SG&A from $4,800M to $5,834M (FY2023–FY2025). ROIC was 4.6% against an 11.2% WACC; incremental ROIC was -0.268. Regulatory-credit revenue fell $770M (28%) after OBBBA. The 2025 CEO award carries $9.82B of unrecognised expense for the probable milestone, plus $105.82B, $120.37B for milestones not judged probable, a catch-up-charge risk. In Q2 2026 the CEO exercised about 304.0M options under the 2018 award, so dilution is under way. Clean checks: Beneish M -2.89 (threshold -1.78), Montier C 3, accrual ratio -0.084 (operating cash $14,747M vs net income $3,794M), negligible goodwill and intangibles, 29 of 29 evaluated identity checks passed. The warranty reserve is being built, not released: 3.9% to 9.1% of revenue (FY2021–FY2025). Working capital is worsening: the cash conversion cycle went from -15.3 to +13.9 days, and inventory jumped in Q1 2026. Credit is very strong: $35.9B net cash, $44.1B liquidity, distance to default 12.39, $1,576M of debt due within a year.

6Execution track record

Execution track record P03_track_record · 11/11 checklist

I sourced 19 promises from Tesla's filings and closed 10 with later-filing evidence; 6 have a timing verdict the filings support. Four were on time, early or on track (Shanghai Model 3 by end-2019, Model Y 'earlier than anticipated', the 2024 restructuring, New York investment targets). Two were late: the 2018 Model 3 weekly targets, and Berlin and Texas, which slipped from 2021 to 2022 while filings said 'progressing as planned'. No row can be checked against budget: the engine has no capex dollar line. Nine rows remain open, mostly new products: Semi (listed since 2018, still pilot production or construction in 2025), Roadster, high-volume in-house cells (still 'developing' in July 2026), Mexico, and the Maxwell and Grohmann synergies. Cybertruck, Robotaxi (launched June 2025) and Cybercab (production began H1 2026) arrived, but the filings never dated them, so delay cannot be measured. No buybacks or dividends; capex took 64.30% of operating cash flow on the decade mean (57.82% in 2025), consistent with stated reinvestment. Goodwill is $257m with no impairment line reported. Average 1-day filing reactions were +4.41% up and -3.49% down (5-day +6.69%, -3.18%); the engine does not flag asymmetry, so there is no evidence misses are punished harder. The stock fell -60.63% at worst in 2020 and -47.64% in 2022 while operating cash flow rose. The 8-K rate fell from 18.86 to 11 a year. Every shareholder lawsuit reviewed was resolved for the defendants; going-private derivative suits remain stayed. 1. Management execution score: 55/100 (JUDGMENT, confidence 0.45; 19 rows, 10 closed, 6 timed, 0 costed). 2. Promise-to-delivery haircut: 0.6 (JUDGMENT, confidence 0.45; about 0.75 for factory and capacity promises, about 0.45 for new products and technology).

  • FACT Row 1, Model 3 ramp. Promised (10-K filed 2018-02-23): 2,500 Model 3 a week by end-Q1 2018 and 5,000 a week by end-Q2 2018. Delivered: output 'exceeded 2,000 vehicles per week for three consecutive weeks' before the April 2018 downtime, and the 5,000 target was moved to 'around the beginning of July 2018' (10-Q filed 2018-05-07). Q3 2018 averaged about 4,300 a week, with 5,300 in the last week of the quarter (10-Q filed 2018-11-02). Cost: not disclosed. Verdict on the filings' own dates: the Q1 target was missed, and 5,000 a week was reached in a single week only by end-Q3 2018, later than promised. 10-K filed 2018-02-23 Item 7 chars 5414-6810 10-Q filed 2018-05-07 Item 2 chars 4324-5529 10-Q filed 2018-11-02 Item 2 chars 5098-5802
  • FACT Row 2, Model 3 rate goals. Promised (10-K filed 2019-02-19): about 7,000 a week at Fremont, sustained, by end-2019. Including Shanghai, 10,000 a week sustained and an annualised output above 500,000 Model 3 at some point between Q4 2019 and Q2 2020. Later filing: only installed capacity is reported (Fremont Model 3 and Model Y combined 400,000; Shanghai 150,000 Model 3; 10-K filed 2020-02-13). No sustained-rate figure was retrieved. Verdict: open. 10-K filed 2019-02-19 Item 1A chars 3687-5087 10-K filed 2020-02-13 Item 7 chars 2394-3786
  • FACT Row 3, Gigafactory Shanghai. Promised (10-K filed 2019-02-19): start Model 3 production for China by end-2019, at a lower capital cost per unit than the Fremont line. Delivered: 'installed annual production capacity for 150,000 Model 3 vehicles' (10-K filed 2020-02-13), and production was started and ramped 'quickly and cost-effectively' (10-K filed 2022-02-07). Verdict: on time. The cost claim is management's own assessment and comes with no figure. 10-K filed 2019-02-19 Item 1A chars 3687-5087 10-K filed 2019-02-19 Item 7 chars 95920-97317 10-K filed 2020-02-13 Item 7 chars 2394-3786 10-K filed 2022-02-07 Item 1 chars 19340-20516
  • FACT Row 4, Model Y. Promised (10-K filed 2019-02-19): volume production by end-2020, with a ramp 'significantly faster than that of Model 3' and lower cost per unit of capacity. 7Forward pipeline and feasibility

Forward pipeline and feasibility P04_pipeline · 10/12 checklist

Nine projects are sourced. Four have started: the Robotaxi service (Austin, June 2025), Cybercab (production from H1 2026), the Texas lithium refinery (running since January 2026) and the cathode plant (ramping). Five are open: Optimus (readying large-scale production; undated, uncosted), Semi (listed since 2018; pilot production 2023-2024), in-house cells (still 'developing' in July 2026), the Houston Megafactory (under construction, undated) and the next-generation platform. Only company-wide cost is disclosed: 2026 capex 'exceed $20 billion' in the January 10-K, raised to 'in excess of $25 billion' in the April and July 10-Qs. No open project has a stated date, so P03's 0.6 haircut cannot produce implied dates. I would weight new products at 0.45 and factory copies at 0.75, P03's own sub-figures. Funding: a one-year need of $25bn is covered. Capacity is $104.96bn at 2.0x net debt to EBITDA (gap -$79.96bn) and $86.19bn at zero net debt (gap -$61.19bn), so no dilution is needed. Option values, with present value set equal to cost because none is disclosed: the autonomy program is worth $11.45bn ($2.90 a share) at 0.8 volatility and $7.87bn ($1.99) at 0.5. Optimus is worth $0.71bn and Semi $0.18bn per $1bn invested. All of it is time value, a bet that uncertainty resolves well. Ten-year scenarios (illustrative DCFs, not P12's drivers): bear $21.74 a share, base $40.56, bull $146.38 (year-10 revenue $578.88bn at a 25% margin; fails two terminal checks). The $362.44 price is above the bull case. The mechanical terminal year matches no case: a flat 9.52% margin with growth climbing to 23.70% in year 10, then 2%. Tesla has made no buybacks; at $362.44 a buyback would retire shares above every value computed here.

8Industry, competition and bubble risk

Industry, competition and bubble risk P05_industry · 12/12 checklist

No filing in the snapshot sizes Tesla's markets, so TAM, SAM and SOM are a data gap, not an estimate. Five-forces scores (JUDGMENT): rivalry 5/5, entry 4/5, substitutes, buyers and suppliers 3/5 each. The car-making profit pool is thin: measured peers' median operating margin is -31.91% trailing (GM 1.08%, Ford -3.77%, Rivian -60.05%, Lucid -263.61%) and -4.90% across seven peers on fiscal-year figures. Tesla's 4.59% ranks first on both bases, but was 16.76% in 2022, and ROIC (4.60%) is below the cost of capital (11.20%). Peers 'out-grow' Tesla only against its fiscal-2025 growth of -2.93%: GM's lead is under one point; Rivian and Lucid buy growth at deeply negative margins in other segments. NIO and Li Auto growth figures are flagged and unusable. BYD, Toyota and Stellantis could not be measured, so the most important rivals are missing. Pricing: the 2025 selling price fell on mix and incentives; the 2026 recovery came from volume with flat cost per unit, and Q2 automotive gross margin was 16.9%, so no sign of pricing power. Storage is the one improving profit pool: unit cost is falling faster than the Megapack price, though cell tariffs threaten that. Vehicle demand is cyclical; margin pressure and regulatory-credit run-off are structural. Tesla is not building inventory (57.15 days); the industry signal cannot be read. Bubble test: EV hardware is not in a bubble (peers near 2.82x EBITDA); the autonomy premium may be, at 232.26x EBITDA and 376.26x earnings, though Tesla funds itself (free cash flow $6,220m). Bubble probability: 0.60 for the autonomy-priced segment, 0.15 for EV hardware; falsifiers are in the findings.

9Macro, policy and geopolitics

Macro, policy and geopolitics P06_macro · 11/11 checklist

The six macro series explain little of TSLA's weekly returns: R² is 10.35% over 155 weekly observations. Only one series clears two sigma, the high-yield spread (beta −0.121, t −2.83). The ten-year yield, the 2s10s curve, breakeven inflation, the dollar and oil show no demonstrated link. The HY spread is tight at 3.25% (+0.14 over one year), so the macro risk the data actually show is credit spreads widening, on top of a market beta of 1.66. Duration from the sensitivity grid (2% terminal growth): $37.23 at 10.20% WACC, $33.17 at 11.20%, $30.02 at 12.20%. The 5.19% ten-year yield (+1.16pp over one year) is already in the WACC. Inflation pass-through: the 0.307 correlation is weak evidence. Tesla absorbed 2022 cost inflation (gross margin 25.60% vs 25.28%), but the margin fell to 18.25% in 2023 and has stayed near that level since, so its pricing power rises and falls with the cycle. H1 2026 revenue: US $23,885m, China $8,859m, other international $17,879m. China's tax footprint is outsized: $751m cash tax against $28m US federal. A 10% adverse FX move is worth $1.70bn, measured before any hedging, and the 2025 FX transaction loss was $407m. OBBBA repealed consumer EV credits, and regulatory-credit revenue fell 67% in Q2 2026. The next exposures are the manufacturing credits (−6.7pp of the tax rate) and critical-mineral eligibility rules. The filer says tariffs have already affected pricing, and some EV and storage-battery parts are hard to source in the US. Scenario judgments: US, China status quo 55%, escalation 30%, de-escalation 15%; further US curtailment of remaining credits 30%; credit-spread shock moderate 28%, severe 12%. P12/P13 should price China volumes and energy margin under escalation, the run-off of credits, and a +100bp WACC case. Gaps: prediction-market and polling data, hedging detail, supplier geography, OBBBA phase-out dates, EU duties.

10Operations and supply chain

Operations and supply chain P07_operations · 8/8 checklist

Tesla's eight primary plants (FY2025 10-K, Item 2) are Gigafactory Texas, Fremont, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg, Gigafactory Shanghai, Megafactory Shanghai, Gigafactory New York (leased) and Megafactory Lathrop (leased). Capacity, utilisation, cost position and age are undisclosed for every plant. The 10-K names lithium and nickel as key battery inputs and flags trade policy and refining capacity; input cost shares and hedging are undisclosed. Through 2025 the 10-Qs repeat one cost story: lower material costs offset by higher tariffs and weaker fixed-cost absorption. The 2021 10-K says most suppliers are single-source; no named supplier or current customer-concentration note was found. The cash conversion cycle moved from negative in FY2021 to about +14 days in FY2025 while revenue fell; finished goods rose sharply in H1 2025. Headcount was 134,785 at FY2025 year-end; trend and union status are undisclosed, and shareholder proposals cite past NLRB findings. Without input cost shares, ±10/20/30% input moves could not be mapped to margin, so three operating-margin stresses were run: mechanical value is $33.17 per share at 9.5%, falling to $26.24 at 7.5%, $19.37 at 5.5% and $12.49 at 3.5%. All stressed runs fail the terminal-share check; read them as direction only. P12 margin risks: tariffs, under-absorbed fixed cost, warranty accrual growth, battery-metal price swings. P13 failure modes: single-site shutdown (Shanghai Q2 2022 precedent), single-source supplier loss, cell or raw-material shortage, recalls and ADAS crash reporting under NHTSA's Standing General Order.

  • FACT The FY2025 10-K lists eight primary manufacturing facilities. Gigafactory Texas (Austin), Fremont, Gigafactory Nevada (Sparks) and Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg (Grunheide) are owned. Tesla owns the buildings at Gigafactory Shanghai and Megafactory Shanghai and holds 50-year land-use rights. Gigafactory New York (Buffalo) and Megafactory Lathrop are leased. 10-K filed 2026-01-29 Item 2 chars 0-1202
  • FACT The FY2025 facility list is identical to the FY2024 list, so the 10-K discloses no new primary manufacturing site for 2025. 10-K filed 2025-01-30 Item 2 chars 0-1202 10-K filed 2026-01-29 Item 2 chars 0-1202
  • INFERENCE Revenue relative to net PP&E (`ppe_utilisation_proxy`) is a rough asset-turnover proxy, not a utilisation rate. With revenue falling in FY2025 and the footprint unchanged, plant utilisation was probably lower than in earlier years. The 10-Qs back this qualitatively by citing lower fixed-cost absorption. confidence 0.60
  • FACT Tesla says battery-cell cost depends partly on lithium, nickel and other metals. Their prices fluctuate, and supply may be unstable because of market conditions, trade policies, refining capacity and global demand. If Tesla cannot make its own cells it may have to curtail production or buy cells from suppliers at potentially higher cost. 10-K filed 2026-01-29 Item 1A chars 14088-15483
  • FACT In Q3 2025, average cost per unit for automotive rose because fixed costs were spread over fewer units, tariffs increased and mix shifted, partly offset by lower material costs. For the nine months, cost per unit fell, with tariffs again partly offsetting. 10-Q filed 2025-10-23 Item 2 chars 21544-22810
  • FACT Megapack cost per unit fell in Q3 2025 on lower raw-material costs and lower manufacturing costs, helped by the Megafactory Shanghai ramp. Higher tariffs partly offset the gain. 10-Q filed 2025-10-23 Item 2 chars 23754-24972
  • FACT In Q2 2022, Tesla took $168 million of idle-capacity charges from the temporary production suspension at Gigafactory Shanghai and the Texas ramp. That is a disclosed precedent for a single-site disruption. 10-Q filed 2022-07-25 Item 2 chars 26435-27826
  • FACT Tesla says it depends on suppliers, the majority of which are single-source, and that a failure to deliver on time, at acceptable price, quality and volume could have a material adverse effect. 10-K filed 2021-02-08 Item 8 chars 81753-83064
  • FACT At December 31, 2020 and 2019, no single entity accounted for 10% or more of accounts receivable. This is the latest customer-concentration statement we retrieved. 10-K filed 2021-02-08 Item 8 chars 81753-83064

These are the proponent's statements, not the company's. A similar proposal appeared in the 2024 proxy. DEF 14A filed 2022-06-23 chars 124950-126055 DEF 14A filed 2024-04-29 chars 354087-355182

  • FACT Tesla must file Early Warning Reports on warranty claims, field reports, deaths and injuries, and foreign recalls. Because the terminal checks fail, the stressed values should be read as direction only. The runs are not mapped to specific ±10/20/30% input-price moves because no input's share of cost of revenue is disclosed. confidence 0.70
  • JUDGMENT Margin risks for P12, in rough order: (1) tariffs on imported components and cells, cited every quarter of 2025; (2) fixed costs spread over fewer units if volumes stall at an unchanged footprint; (3) warranty accrual growth; (4) a reversal of the lower battery-metal costs that helped 2024 and 2025. Operational failure modes for P13: a single-plant shutdown, a single-source supplier failure, a cell or raw-material shortage, and recalls or ADAS regulatory action. confidence 0.60

11Management and governance

Management and governance P08_governance · 11/11 checklist

Insider dealing is neutral to slightly negative, and almost all of it was planned. Over 180 days, the window used for scoring, there were no open-market buys. There were 19 open-market sells by two people, and 89.47% of them ran under 10b5-1 plans. The 365-day window looks the same: four sellers, no buyers and 92.31% planned. The 90-day window holds a single small unplanned sale by one person. Insider-sentiment score: -10 on a -100 to +100 scale (JUDGMENT, 0.6). Pay and control matter much more than the trading. The Delaware Supreme Court reinstated the 2018 CEO award. Musk then exercised about 304.0m options in Q2 2026, net-settling about 17.5m shares. The resulting shares cannot vest before 19 January 2028 and must then be held for five years. The 96m-share 2025 Interim Award was forfeited under the 'no double dip' rule. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7m restricted shares in 12 tranches. Its targets run from a $2.0 trillion market value to $8.5 trillion and up to $400bn of adjusted EBITDA. At 31 March 2026, $105.82bn to $120.37bn of its cost had not been booked because the milestones are not yet probable: a real claim the income statement omits. Unearned shares vote in proportion to other shareholders. Musk owned 20.3% at end-2025, and the September 2025 proxy showed about 236m of his shares pledged. Tesla moved to Texas and in May 2025 adopted a bylaw: only shareholders holding at least 3% can bring a derivative suit. Tesla put $2.00bn into Musk-affiliated SpaceX (originally xAI). The board calls every director independent except Elon and Kimbal Musk. PwC has audited Tesla since 2005. Governance quality: 35/100 (JUDGMENT, 0.55). Incentives are steep and price-aligned, but checks on the controlling holder are weak.

Mechanical transactions (insider_365d_mechanical_transactions) are kept separate and are not counted as selling. confidence 0.75
  • INFERENCE The only discretionary sale in the last 90 days was a single unplanned open-market sale by one person (insider_90d_open_market_sells, insider_90d_planned_share_of_sells, insider_90d_distinct_sellers). Its value (insider_90d_sell_value) is tiny next to insider holdings, so it is noise, not a signal. confidence 0.65

The score is held near neutral because the selling is concentrated and pre-scheduled, and no insider is buying in the open market. confidence 0.60

12Sentiment, positioning and flows

Sentiment, positioning and flows P09_sentiment · 9/9 checklist

Positioning is neither crowded nor heavily shorted. All three available sources are partial. Short interest is low: about 1.80% of shares outstanding, 1.94 days to cover, and at the 36th percentile of its five-year range (`short_share_of_shares_outstanding`, `short_days_to_cover`, `short_percentile_5y`). It is up 16.5% over six months but down 7.7% over twelve (`short_change_6m`, `short_change_12m`). We read it as hedging plus residual bears, not a building bear case, and squeeze risk is low. FINRA data lags about eight business days, and borrow fee and utilisation are missing. The 13F picture is the weakest source. Filers report 25.86% of shares outstanding (`holder_share_of_shares_outstanding`). That figure is understated: it is long-only, 45 days stale, leaves out Musk's roughly 20.3% stake (he files no 13F), and drops 178 rows with impossible prices (`holder_rows_dropped`). The engine flags 360 bad positions, including T. Rowe Price and CalSTRS. Do not read the 11.06% quarter-on-quarter fall (`holder_quarter_on_quarter_change`) as institutions selling. The top five filers hold 44.7% and the top ten 56.5% (`holder_top_five_share`, `holder_top_ten_share`), most likely passive index managers. Insider sales were small and almost all made under 10b5-1 plans, consistent with P08. The main fragility is not positioning. It is the controlling holder (Musk, with about 236m shares pledged) and volatility of 59.6% a year with a 73.6% maximum drawdown (`annual_volatility`, `max_drawdown`). Low short interest means no short-covering support on bad news and no squeeze on good news. Composite sentiment score: about -7 on a -100 to +100 scale. Weights are holders 40%, shorts 35% and insiders 25%, with components -15, +5 and -10. JUDGMENT, confidence 0.4; the engine should recompute. 13Technical and quant profile

Technical and quant profile P10_technical · 9/9 checklist

TSLA's market data shows a high-beta stock with falling momentum and no clear trend. It sits in the lower third of its 52-week range (range_position_52w, from_52w_high), below its 20-, 100- and 200-day averages and slightly above its 50-day. ADX near 15 means no trend, RSI 46 is neutral and the MACD histogram is slightly negative: range-bound with a downward lean. These readings describe the chart; they do not predict. Momentum_12_1 is negative and the stock lagged SPY (excess_vs_SPY). Trailing-year alpha is negative and beta rose to 2.20 from 1.66 over the full window, so recent returns tracked the market more closely (y1_r_squared vs r_squared). Five of six factor loadings clear t=2: market 1.45 (t 25.5) and strongly negative HML, RMW and CMA, the profile of an unprofitable, heavily investing growth stock. SMB only just clears t=2; momentum (t 1.54) is not demonstrated. Factor R² is 0.327, so most return variance is stock-specific. In stress replays TSLA lost much more than the benchmark in COVID 2020 and the 2022 rate shock, and gained slightly in the 2023 regional-bank stress. No 2008 replay or recovery times were computed, so the −73.6% maximum drawdown understates the holding experience. Worst-day losses exceed what a normal distribution implies (historical CVaR worse than parametric). Without options or microstructure data, the option-implied distribution cannot be compared with the house distribution. The house Monte Carlo (P10 $20.97 to P90 $48.16) lies entirely below the $362.44 price, consistent with P06's DCF grid; P12, P13 and P15 should check for a units or share-count problem before relying on it. No price target is set here.

14Legal, ESG and tail risk

Legal, ESG and tail risk P11_legal · 8/8 checklist

Legal: the 2018 CEO-award case (Tornetta) has been reversed in Tesla's favor. The Delaware Supreme Court reinstated the award, the Court of Chancery entered a final order on 18 March 2026, and Musk's 96-million-share 2025 interim award was forfeited on 21 April 2026. The directors'-pay settlement was affirmed on 30 January 2026, with the fee cut from $176m to $71m. Tesla's record in securities and governance cases is strong: it won the going-private jury verdict and the SolarCity and Model S cases, and the SEC financing probe was closed. Product liability is different. In Benavides, a jury awarded $129m compensatory damages (Tesla 33% at fault) plus $200m punitive damages over a 2019 Autopilot crash. Post-trial motions were denied and the case is on appeal to the Eleventh Circuit, yet Tesla has booked only an 'immaterial accrual'. The FSD/ADAS class action has a certified California class, stayed while the Ninth Circuit hears Tesla's appeal of the certification. NHTSA, NTSB, SEC and DOJ inquiries cover Autopilot, FSD and Robotaxi. Tesla is 'unable to reasonably estimate the possible loss or range of loss' unless noted, and no range is disclosed for any pending matter. Regulation and ESG: the OBBBA (July 2025) cut certain IRA tax credits and removed certain regulatory-credit penalties, putting credit sales at risk. Physical risk: Fremont and Nevada are seismically active, Shanghai is flood-prone, and Texas was hit by the Q1 2021 winter storm. Key person: Tesla is 'highly dependent' on Musk, who does not work for it full time. Tail inventory (qualitative JUDGMENTs): an ADAS or Robotaxi enforcement action; Autopilot punitive verdicts multiplying; Musk leaving; a disaster at Shanghai or Fremont. Default is not a tail risk (distance_to_default). The share of holders who would be forced sellers on an ESG downgrade cannot be measured.

  • FACT Benavides v. Tesla (S.D. Fla.): on 1 August 2025 a jury found against Tesla in a product-liability trial over a 2019 crash involving Autopilot that killed one person and injured others. It awarded $129 million in total compensatory damages, found the driver 67% and Tesla 33% at fault, and awarded $200 million in punitive damages. 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 Item 1 chars 67983-69139
  • FACT Where Benavides stands: the court denied Tesla's post-trial motions on 19 February 2026, Tesla filed its notice of appeal on 16 March 2026 and its opening brief with the Eleventh Circuit on 2 July 2026. The company 'has recorded an immaterial accrual'. 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 Item 1 chars 67983-69139 10-Q filed 2026-04-23 Item 1 chars 66533-67710
  • JUDGMENT An 'immaterial accrual' against a verdict that includes $200 million in punitive damages shows management expects to win on appeal. The bigger risk is not this one case but the precedent: if the verdict stands, juries in other Autopilot crash cases have a template for punitive damages that Tesla does not quantify. confidence 0.60
  • FACT The FSD/ADAS consumer class action (N.D. Cal., filed 14 September 2022) seeks damages for everyone who bought or leased from Tesla since 1 January 2016. A limited class of California consumers not bound by arbitration was certified on 18 August 2025. The Ninth Circuit agreed on 18 December 2025 to hear Tesla's appeal of that order, and the district court stayed the case on 5 January 2026. An earlier request for an injunction to stop use of the term 'Full Self-Driving Capability' was denied on 30 September 2023. 10-Q filed 2026-04-23 Item 1 chars 63167-64564 10-Q filed 2026-04-23 Item 1 chars 64364-65764
  • FACT For its product-related claims Tesla states: 'We are unable to reasonably estimate the possible loss or range of loss, if any, associated with these claims, unless noted.' No loss range is disclosed for any pending matter in the passages retrieved. 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 Item 1 chars 67983-69139 10-K filed 2026-01-29 Item 8 chars 160022-161013

Topics include vehicle incidents, Autopilot and FSD Capability, Robotaxi, compliance, finance, data privacy, personnel and related parties. Tesla says that to its knowledge no agency has concluded that any wrongdoing occurred, that it cannot predict the outcome, and that an enforcement action could have a material adverse impact. 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 Item 1 chars 69639-70895 10-K filed 2026-01-29 Item 8 chars 161513-162769

  • JUDGMENT Tail event 1, a federal enforcement action that restricts or recalls FSD or Robotaxi (NHTSA or DOJ, both named in the investigations disclosure). Probability: low but not remote. 15Valuation

Valuation P12_valuation · 10/10 checklist

No defensible cash-flow forecast gets to TSLA's $362.44 price. The mechanical DCF gives $33.17 (WACC 11.20%, all terminal checks passed). Its drivers are generous, not biased low: a 9.5% margin from year 1 against 4.6% in FY2025, growth rising to 23.7% by year 10 against -2.9% in FY2025, and a 19.5% terminal ROIC, though P02 found ROIC below WACC. My justified runs all pass the checks. Base (15-year) $25.62: growth recovers to 10% then fades, margin rises from 4% to 10%, sales-to-capital 1.8, terminal ROIC 12%. Bull (15-year) $111.20: growth fades from 25% to 4%, margin rises from 6% to 20%, terminal ROIC 20%. Bear (10-year) $15.04: 2% growth at a flat 4% margin. The reverse DCF says the price needs 57.6% annual revenue growth at the mechanical margin, and at mechanical growth no margin up to 90% gets there. A deliberate stress case needs $1.27T of revenue by year 10, a 25% margin and a 30% terminal ROIC. It fails two checks and still gives $347.32. That gap is the thesis: the price pays for autonomy, robotaxi and Optimus outcomes far beyond Tesla's best year, while revenue has stalled and margins have fallen for three years. EPV is $13.90 and the LBO ceiling $26.94. Monte Carlo around the mechanical drivers gives P10–P90 of $20.59–$51.38, with a 0.0007 chance of value above the price. LTM comps imply $13.02 (EV/EBITDA), $34.78 (P/E) and $45.35 (EV/revenue), indicative only with 4 usable peers. The most generous WACC/growth corner gives $49.23, so the discount rate doesn't decide it. Fair value: $15.04–$111.20, centred on $25.62. Limits: the Monte Carlo and the grid use mechanical drivers; fiscal-year comps and the 20-F and BYD peers were unavailable; future CEO-award dilution may be missing from the 3,949M share count.

  • FACT Cost of capital: WACC 11.20%, cost of equity 11.26%, risk-free rate 5.19%, equity risk premium 4.2%, Blume-adjusted beta 1.45 (raw 1.66), pre-tax cost of debt 1.91% (after tax 1.40%). Market weights are 99.43% equity and 0.57% debt. wacc, cost_of_equity, risk_free, equity_risk_premium, beta_blume, beta_raw, cost_of_debt, after_tax_cost_of_debt, equity_weight, debt_weight
  • JUDGMENT 11.20% is a defensible rate. With almost no debt in the market weights, WACC is effectively the cost of equity. A Blume beta near 1.45 suits a cyclical, capital-intensive automaker with a volatile stock. The raw beta of 1.66 would argue for a higher rate, not a lower one. confidence 0.65

Scenarios, targets and catalysts P13_scenarios · 10/11 checklist
  • FACT Super-bear scenario at the run_dcf drivers: revenue falls 5%, 5% and 3%, then grows 2%; operating margin 2% rising to 3%; sales-to-capital 1.5; terminal ROIC 8%. Value per share $14.56. It fails the terminal-ROIC-versus-WACC check: an 8% ROIC sits below the 11.20% WACC, so growth destroys value. That failure is intended, because the scenario describes value destruction. super-bear run
  • INFERENCE How the super-bear happens: regulatory-credit income runs off after the OBBBA, price cuts continue, deliveries fall back after the 2026 recovery, and the Benavides verdict is upheld and followed by similar Autopilot verdicts. Autonomy earns nothing material. Early warnings: Q3 or Q4 2026 revenue down year on year, automotive gross margin below Q2's 16.9%, and credit revenue collapsing. confidence 0.60
  • FACT Bear scenario: 2% growth and a flat 4% operating margin over 10 years, with sales-to-capital and terminal ROIC at their mechanical values. Value per share $16.22. All terminal checks pass. P12's bear on the same headline drivers gave $15.04. bear run
  • INFERENCE How the bear happens: Tesla stays a car-and-storage company with a stalled top line and margins stuck near FY2025 levels, while Cybercab and Robotaxi keep slipping. Early warnings: deliveries flat in the second half of 2026, no new production status for Cybercab in the 10-K, and operating margin unchanged. confidence 0.60
  • FACT Base scenario: growth starts at 10% and fades to 3% over 15 years; margin rises from 4% to 10%; sales-to-capital 1.8; terminal ROIC 12%; tax at the mechanical 15.7%. Value per share $24.74. All checks pass. Terminal value is 61.6% of enterprise value, and free cash flow is negative for the first three years. base run
  • FACT Tesla reports producing about 860 thousand and delivering about 838 thousand consumer vehicles in the first half of 2026, and deploying 22.3 GWh of energy storage over the same period. 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 Item 2 chars 1400-2443
  • INFERENCE How the base happens: the 2026 volume recovery and storage growth carry revenue for several years, and margin rebuilds slowly as Robotaxi adds a modest contribution. Early warnings: second-half 2026 deliveries keep pace with the first half, storage deployments keep rising, and operating margin moves up from the FY2025 level. confidence 0.55
  • FACT Bull scenario: growth fades from 25% to 4% over 15 years; margin rises from 6% to 20%; terminal ROIC 20%; tax and sales-to-capital at mechanical values. Value per share $102.71. All checks pass. Year-15 revenue is about $706bn. bull run
  • INFERENCE How the bull happens: paid driverless Robotaxi service and FSD software become material, high-margin revenue lines, and Cybercab reaches volume production. Early warnings: Robotaxi or FSD revenue disclosed separately and growing, Cybercab listed as in production, and operating margin reaching double digits within two years. confidence 0.50
  • FACT Super-bull scenario: growth fades from 40% to 5% over 15 years; margin rises from 8% to 25%; sales-to-capital 2.5; terminal ROIC 25%. Year-10 revenue is about $1.17T. super-bull run
  • INFERENCE How the super-bull happens: Robotaxi scales across many markets without safety drivers, and Optimus is sold externally in volume. Early warnings: regulators approve driverless operation broadly, Optimus revenue is recognized, and margins jump within a few quarters. confidence 0.50
  • JUDGMENT Scenario probabilities: super-bear 10%, bear 25%, base 40%, bull 20%, super-bull 5%. Total 100%. The base gets the most weight because it matches the 2026 volume recovery while respecting three years of falling margins. The super-bull gets only 5% because it fails two plausibility checks. confidence 0.50
  • INFERENCE All five scenario values sit below the price, so any set of weights gives a probability-weighted value below the price and a negative expected return on fundamentals. With these weights, the four scenarios that pass their checks or are deliberately bearish (90% of the probability) are each worth less than a third of the price. The engine has not computed an exact weighted figure or targets by horizon. confidence 0.85

18cPrimary research plan

Primary research plan P2C_primary_research · 9/9 checklist

This plan lists research still to be done. It contains no evidence. It targets the weakest points of this run, all undisclosed in the filings. (1) Automotive economics without regulatory credits: net selling price after incentives, cost per vehicle and warranty cost per unit. (2) Whether the H1 2026 delivery rebound is real demand or bought with discounts, financing offers and channel inventory. (3) What FSD and Robotaxi actually earn: attach rate, subscription retention and the paid driverless service, on which the autonomy-priced valuation depends. (4) Energy storage: Megapack pricing against Chinese integrators, cell-tariff pass-through and order-book depth. (5) Position against BYD, Toyota and Stellantis, which the comps could not measure. (6) Whether rising warranty and ADAS-liability costs persist. The plan covers twenty expert-call questions, four channel checks, a three-market customer survey, a teardown producing a BOM cost estimate, and repeatable field signals with thresholds. Every item names a refuting result. Pending until done: P01 value drivers 2, 3 and 5 and its warranty point; P05's no-pricing-power and autonomy-bubble verdicts and the BYD/Toyota/Stellantis gap; P07's tariff and fixed-cost absorption risks and single-source supplier failure mode; P11's tail risk of multiplying Autopilot verdicts. Highest priority: whether automotive gross margin excluding credits is stable or still falling, then whether FSD is used and paid for, which is evidence the autonomy premium needs and lacks. All questions use public information only and go to former employees, customers, dealers and competitors; none asks for unreported current-period results or confidential terms.

  • JUDGMENT The uncertainty that matters most is whether automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits is stable or still falling. Selling price after incentives, cost per vehicle and warranty cost per unit are all undisclosed. The engine's gross_margin cannot separate pricing, credits and cost, so the channel checks and expert questions Q1–Q3 carry the most weight. confidence 0.70
  • JUDGMENT The second priority is evidence that FSD and Robotaxi actually earn money. The autonomy-priced valuation segment has no disclosed attach rate or retention data behind it. If the survey and the hands-on FSD test refute monetisation, that would move valuation more than any vehicle-side finding. confidence 0.60
  • INFERENCE Channel inventory checks are the only way to test the days_inventory_outstanding reading in the field. The industry-level inventory signal could not be read because BYD, Toyota and Stellantis have no usable fundamentals in the snapshot. confidence 0.65
  • FACT Tesla's supply-chain risk disclosure has said that most of its direct suppliers are single source. This plan treats that as dated evidence, to be re-tested in Q10. 10-Q filed 2016-11-02 Item 1A chars 14253-15246

  • JUDGMENT Question for management: what caused the upward revisions to existing warranty reserves? Are they specific campaigns or a change in fleet-wide failure-rate assumptions? confidence 0.55
  • JUDGMENT Question for management: how deep is the energy-storage order backlog, and how much of cell tariff costs is passed through in Megapack contracts? confidence 0.55

Glossary

Every term this report uses, in plain English, with what it does not tell you (§39).

Accrual ratio
Earnings not backed by cash, as a share of assets. Persistently high accruals are the most-studied warning sign in accounting research (Sloan 1996).
ADV
Average daily volume. How much of the stock trades in a normal day, which bounds how large a position can be entered or exited.
Altman Z
A bankruptcy-risk score from five balance-sheet ratios (Altman 1968). Above about 3 is the safe zone for a manufacturer.
Alpha
Return not explained by the market or by the factor model being used. It is defined relative to a model, so it changes when the model does.
Beneish M
An earnings-manipulation score from eight accounting ratios (Beneish 1999). Above -1.78 is the flag, which is a screen and not a verdict.
Beta
How much the stock has moved for a one-percent move in the benchmark. Measured over a window, so it is a description of the past.
Blume adjustment
Shrinking a measured beta toward one, because high and low betas both drift back over time (Blume 1971).
Comps
Comparable-company analysis: valuing a company at the multiples its peers trade on, which answers “what is this worth to the market”, not “what is this worth”.
Days to cover
Short interest divided by average daily volume: how many days of normal trading it would take the shorts to buy back their position.
DCF
Discounted cash flow. The value of a business as the cash it will produce, discounted for time and risk. Its answer is only as good as its drivers.
Distance to default
How many standard deviations of asset value separate a company from the point where its assets equal its debts (Merton 1974).
DuPont decomposition
Splitting return on equity into margin, asset turnover and leverage, so a rising return can be read as efficiency or as borrowing.
EPV
Earnings power value: the business valued on current earnings with no growth. A floor that does not depend on a forecast (Greenwald).
EV
Enterprise value: the value of the whole business, debt included, before subtracting what the lenders own.
Factor exposure
How much of a return is explained by known drivers - size, value, profitability, momentum - rather than by the company itself (Fama and French).
FCF
Free cash flow: cash from operations less the capital spending needed to keep the business running.
Kelly fraction
The bet size that maximises long-run growth given an edge. A raw Kelly above one says the inputs are too confident, not that leverage is advisable.
LBO ceiling
The most a leveraged buyer could pay and still earn its required return. Another floor under the price, not a forecast.
Market impact
The price move caused by trading itself. Estimated here with a square-root law, which is an approximation and never a quotable cost.
Monte Carlo
Running a valuation thousands of times with drawn inputs, to get a distribution instead of a single number. The distribution inherits the assumptions.
NOPAT
Net operating profit after tax: operating profit as if the company had no debt, which is what a DCF discounts.
Point-in-time
Using only information published on or before the analysis date. Without it a backtest learns from the future and looks brilliant.
Reverse DCF
Solving for the growth or margin the current price implies, which turns “is it cheap” into “what would have to be true”.
ROIC
Return on invested capital. Above the cost of capital, growth creates value; below it, growth destroys value.
Sales-to-capital
How much revenue each unit of invested capital supports, used to turn a growth forecast into a capital-spending forecast (Damodaran).
Sharpe ratio
Return per unit of volatility. It treats upside and downside volatility alike, which flatters strategies that lose rarely and badly.
Short interest
Shares sold short and not yet bought back, reported twice a month by the exchanges with a lag.
Terminal value
The value of everything beyond the forecast window. Where most of a DCF usually sits, which is why its share of the total is checked.
WACC
Weighted average cost of capital: the blended return debt and equity holders require, and the rate a DCF discounts at.
13F
The quarterly holdings report large institutions file 45 days after quarter end. Late, and only institutions.

Disclaimer

This is research output, not investment advice, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any security. It was produced by an automated engine from free public data as of the analysis date above.

Model limitations worth holding in mind. Every forward number is a projection from a model whose drivers are stated and arguable, not a forecast. The scores are uncalibrated until the backtest in M7, so an 80 does not yet mean anything empirical. The data is free data: no consensus estimates, no options chain, no transcripts, no market-size research, no borrow costs, and 13F holdings are 45 days stale. Everything the engine could not get is listed under “what we did not analyze” rather than estimated.
